countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.

universities.name: Sharda University
universities.summary: Sharda University is a state private university in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, in the Delhi NCR, established under a 2009 Uttar Pradesh Act. Its single campus teaches engineering, computing, business, design, pharmacy, media, law, sciences and health programmes in English, and admits international students through a dedicated International Relations Division.
universities.campusLifestyle: Teaching is on one residential campus at Knowledge Park-III, Greater Noida, which Sharda describes as 63 acres with more than 19,200 students from over 95 countries and more than 1,047 faculty. The central library holds about 1.4 lakh books, and school libraries open 8 am to 7 pm, longer during examinations. The campus network runs at 1 Gbps through two ISPs with over 200 access points including hostels. Sharda Hospital is on campus, and the university runs the Suno Sharda 90.8 FM community radio.
universities.cityProfile: Greater Noida is in Gautam Budh Nagar district of Uttar Pradesh, within the Delhi National Capital Region. Sharda states the campus is about an hour's drive from Delhi International Airport, which is the arrival airport it asks new students to book; the International Relations Division arranges airport pickup when flight details are sent at least two weeks ahead. University buses run fixed morning routes from across Delhi, Noida and Faridabad for a separate transport fee. Summer temperatures run 30-45C and winter 5-25C, with winter from around November, so warm bedding and clothing are needed. Mains power is 240 V with two- and three-pin sockets. Everyday items are sold at campus tuck shops and markets within about 5 km. Immigration registration is handled at FRO Noida or FRRO New Delhi.
universities.practicalExposure: Recognition at programme level is specific. The National Board of Accreditation lists Sharda's B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering, Electrical and Electronics Engineering and Biotechnology on its Tier I (Washington Accord) register to 30 June 2028, the MBA on its Management PG register to 30 June 2028, and the B.Pharm on its Pharmacy UG register to 31 December 2028. Several 2026-27 programmes are built with named partners: B.Tech (CSE) Cyber Security and Forensics with EC-Council, B.Tech (CSE) Full Stack Development with Xebia Academic Alliance, B.Tech (EEE) Advanced Electric Vehicle with L&T EduTech, and B.Com International Accounting and Finance with ACCA, UK. B.Tech curricula include project-based learning each year, three summer internships and two capstone semesters, and the three-year media and psychology degrees end in an apprenticeship semester. Sharda reports more than 330 functional MoUs for semester exchange and credit transfer, with partners including Curtin University (Australia), Taipei Medical University (Taiwan), the University of Bremen (Germany) and the University of Malta.
universities.hostelOverview: Rooms are allotted first-come-first-served on payment. Sharda's international accommodation page, still labelled session 2022-23, lists annual per-student rates including food: USD 3,800 for a double AC room, USD 3,100 for a double AC room with shared washroom, USD 2,800 for a double non-AC room and USD 2,300 for a double non-AC room with shared washroom. A refundable security deposit of USD 300 (AC) or USD 200 (non-AC) applies. All hostel residents must eat in the university mess, and no refund is given once a room is occupied. Sharda's 2026 domestic hostel schedule runs INR 1,24,000-2,38,000 a year including mess, from 1 August to 31 May.
universities.dietarySupport: Hostel meals come from a separate hostel mess with vegetarian and non-vegetarian options, and mess charges are built into the hostel rate. The campus also has cafeterias, the Lego House fast-food restaurant and a grocery store for staples. Hostel residents get complimentary laundry of 5 kg x 20 washes per academic year, and may add a room cooler or refrigerator on payment of charges fixed by the Inter-Hostel Administration.
universities.safetyOverview: Sharda states that the campus, hostels, parking and academic areas are guarded 24x7 by outsourced security agencies with armed guards, and a centralised command and control centre monitors about 1,450 CCTV cameras. Each hostel has a warden and a faculty-in-charge. Emergency vans and ambulances are based on campus, with Sharda Hospital on site.
universities.studentSupport: The International Relations Division checks documents at reporting, registers students, and guides FRO/FRRO registration, visa extensions and residence-permit changes. New arrivals get a free medical check-up at Sharda Hospital and a medical-insurance card. IRD also helps open an Indian bank account. University ID cards are issued about 10 days after registration. Confidential counselling is available for personal and study-related concerns.

faq.question: Is Sharda University public or private?
faq.answer: Private. Sharda University is a state private university established by the Uttar Pradesh legislature through Act No. 14 of 2009 and notified on 24 March 2009, run under the non-profit Sharda Education Trust. UGC lists it in its State-wise List of Private Universities for Uttar Pradesh.

faq.question: What language are programmes taught in?
faq.answer: English. Sharda's international FAQ gives English as the medium of instruction, and all seven programmes listed here are taught in English throughout. Sharda also sells a six-month Certificate of Proficiency (English) at USD 1,000 and a one-year advanced certificate at USD 3,000 for students who want extra language support.

faq.question: What marks do international applicants need?
faq.answer: Sharda publishes one rule for international applicants to all programmes: at least 50 per cent in the qualifying examination and having studied the prerequisite subjects for the chosen programme. Subjects are not listed separately for international applicants; the same programme pages' national rules name Physics and Mathematics for B.Tech CSE, Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics for B.Tech ECE, PCM or PCB for B.Pharm, and a bachelor's degree for the MBA. PhD entry needs a relevant master's with 55 per cent.

faq.question: Do international students sit SUAT, JEE or CAT?
faq.answer: No. Sharda's admission FAQ says Foreign/NRI-quota admission is based on marks in the qualifying examination, while SUAT, JEE Main ranks and MAT/CAT/XAT scores belong to the Indian-national route. Sharda does reserve the right to assess a candidate through group discussion or personal interview before final admission.

faq.question: Is there an English test requirement such as IELTS or TOEFL?
faq.answer: Sharda does not publish an IELTS or TOEFL minimum for international applicants. Its domestic programme rules ask for proficiency in English communication, and teaching is in English, so applicants from non-English-medium schools should plan for the English proficiency certificate courses Sharda offers.

faq.question: How much does it cost in total?
faq.answer: Tuition for 2026-27 is published in US dollars per year: for example USD 4,200 for B.Tech CSE, USD 4,000 for B.Tech ECE, B.Des and B.Pharm, USD 3,800 for BA Psychology, USD 3,400 for BA Journalism and USD 6,000 for the MBA. Add USD 500 in procedural charges in year one and USD 250 a year after that, then hostel with food of USD 2,300-3,800 a year on the last published international schedule (2022-23), plus a refundable USD 200-300 deposit.

faq.question: Does my nationality change the fee?
faq.answer: Yes. Nationals of Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh and NRIs from GCC countries pay the same fee structure as Indian students, in rupees, plus an INR 30,000 admission fee, INR 6,000 per semester examination fee and INR 15,000 annual registration from year two. All other international students pay the USD rate. Fees can be paid in US dollars or the equivalent in rupees.

faq.question: Are the scholarships guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Sharda's fee list shows 20 or 50 per cent scholarships against many programmes, but its terms say scholarships are merit-based, apply to tuition only, are confirmed only after original transcripts are verified at reporting, and continue only with regular attendance, progress and good conduct. Only one benefit applies if several are available, and some programmes, such as B.Pharm, show no scholarship.

faq.question: How do I apply?
faq.answer: Apply online through Sharda's international application page. The International Relations Division checks eligibility and issues an offer letter; you then pay USD 500 and email the proof to global@sharda.ac.in. Sharda then issues an Admission Letter / Visa Letter, which you use to apply for a student visa endorsed to Sharda at the nearest Indian mission, allowing 3-8 weeks for processing.

faq.question: When is the intake and the application deadline?
faq.answer: There is one main intake a year. Sharda accepts international applications from January to July and gives 31 July as the last date for Foreign/NRI-quota applications. In the 2026-27 first-year calendar, engineering, computing, business, design and media students reported on 17 August with classes from 31 August, while humanities and pharmacy students reported 24-29 August with classes from 7 September.

faq.question: Do I need an AIU equivalence certificate?
faq.answer: Sharda accepts qualifications recognised by the Association of Indian Universities for equivalence. If your school-leaving or degree qualification is not AIU-recognised, you must provide equivalence proof from the Indian High Commission or Consulate in your country, or another statutory body. Sharda's first-year procedural charge includes AIU equivalence assistance.

faq.question: What do Sharda's accreditations cover?
faq.answer: NAAC accredits the whole university at A+ (CGPA 3.27, Cycle 2, declared January 2023). NBA accreditation is programme-specific: B.Tech ECE, EEE and Biotechnology and the MBA run to 30 June 2028, and B.Pharm to 31 December 2028. The NBA periods for B.Tech Computer Science, Civil and Mechanical Engineering ended on 30 June 2026. In NIRF 2025 Sharda ranks 87 among universities and 57 in pharmacy.

faq.question: Can I work in India while studying, and what happens after arrival?
faq.answer: No work is allowed: the Bureau of Immigration bars employment and business activity on a student visa, and Sharda says its visa cannot be used for employment. After arrival you report to the International Relations Division, have a free medical check at Sharda Hospital, and, unless you are Nepali or Bhutanese, register with FRO Noida or FRRO New Delhi within 14 days.

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission (UGC) - official site
evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. Corroborated by the Study in India portal Indian Higher Education page, which states all institutions are governed by the Ministry of Education.

evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
evidence.sourceLabel: National Medical Commission (NMC) - official site

evidence.claimText: India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Onboarding & FRRO
evidence.internalNotes: The portal adds its own disclaimer that document requirements differ across countries and must be confirmed with the nearest Indian embassy.

evidence.claimText: Admission for Foreign Nationals, OCIs, PIOs and NRIs to undergraduate engineering, architecture and planning programmes at NITs, IIEST, IIITs, SPAs and other centrally funded technical institutes runs through the Ministry of Education DASA scheme, and for the 2026-27 year admission is on the basis of JEE (Main) 2026. DASA seats are supernumerary and capped at up to 15 per cent of a programme's total seats. IITs are outside the DASA scheme.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Brochure DASA 2026 (UG), Central Seat Allocation Board / Ministry of Education
evidence.internalNotes: The qualifying-exam basis has changed between cycles (SAT in earlier cycles, JEE Main for 2026-27). Never state the accepted exam without naming the admission year. Corroborated by dasanit.org, which describes DASA as an MoE scheme for Foreign Nationals, PIOs, OCIs and NRIs to NITs, CFTIs and other premier technical institutions other than IITs.

evidence.claimText: Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India and Foreign Nationals are eligible to appear in NEET (UG) and are eligible for admission to medical and dental colleges subject to the rules of the respective State Governments, institutions and the Government of India. Foreign applicants must upload documentary proof of nationality with the application and are directed to confirm eligibility with the competent state and counselling authorities.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Bulletin NEET (UG)-2026, National Testing Agency
evidence.internalNotes: Chapter 6, sections 1-2. No India medical page may present a NEET-free route. Eligibility is explicitly conditional on state and institution rules, so it varies by college.

evidence.claimText: The National Assessment and Accreditation Council, established in 1994 as an autonomous institution of the UGC, assesses and accredits Indian higher education institutions. evidence.internalNotes: NIRF corroborated separately at https://www.nirfindia.org/Home (MoE, launched 29 September 2015). Use a NAAC grade or NIRF rank only with the assessment or ranking year stated.
